reader.requirement: At --std 85 every REPLACE statement is applied to the text that results after all COPY statements are processed: a REPLACE never changes a COPY statement's own operands, its pseudo-text-1 matches text words brought in by COPY (including a match spanning source and library text), and a REPLACE statement written in library text takes effect.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.ReplaceScopeEndsWithSeparatelyCompiledProgram (scope end, GR3), ReplaceAnywhere2002 (SR1 separator period), ReplaceAlsoLast2002 (ALSO/LAST refused at 85); the COPY-then-REPLACE order is not switched

reader.edition-search: Manipulate renders the whole COPY-expanded text (run.Render) and only then calls ApplyReplaceStatements, for every dialectLevel; grep of dialectLevel/EditionInfo in ConditionalCompilationProcessor.Manipulate finds no edition switch on the order.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the order (COPY first, REPLACE over the expanded text) is the same at 85 and 2023; 85 differs only in REPLACE's own phrase and placement gates
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f28_03 covers REPLACE acting on copied text; not exercised: a REPLACE operand naming the COPY text-name, a match spanning source and library text, a REPLACE written inside library text

probes.expected: REPLACE ==c1lit== BY ==c2lit== does not redirect COPY c1lit (COPY first): LIB; =="Q" "LIB"== matches across source and copied text: JOINED; REPLACE inside copied library text applies to later source: YY

probes.printed: COBOL0900 REPLACE not preceded by a separator period requires COBOL-2002 (§1985:XII.3.3 SR1); COBOL0900 REPLACE ALSO requires COBOL-2002

citations.check: OK  §1985:XII.3.4 GR4  (║3.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR4

reader.notes: ConditionalCompilationProcessor.Manipulate renders the conditional-compilation and COPY driver over the whole text (recursively into copybooks) and applies ApplyReplaceStatements once over the expanded result, so REPLACE sees only post-COPY text. FindStatementKeyword walks text words, so COPY statements are recognized wherever a character-string stands before REPLACE runs.

refuter.evidence: run_probe --std 85 r2cpr.cob (runs/r2cpr-002): a COPY written inside REPLACE pseudo-text-1 and pseudo-text-2 (legal by §1985:XII.2.3 SR7, no rule bars a COPY inside a REPLACE) is processed first: DISPLAY "LIB" -> NEW, DISPLAY "X1" -> LIB, and REPLACE matches the output of a COPY REPLACING ('ZZ' -> ZOK). The first run (r2cpr-001) wrote ==COPY with no space and was refused COBOL2451, correctly by §1985:XII.2.3 SR2. r2op.cob (runs/r2op-001): REPLACE =='LIB'== and ==r1lit== do not alter a COPY's REPLACING operand or text-name (CCC, RRRRRR), REPLACE OFF ends it (LIB). cite.py: OK §1985:XII.3.4 GR4 the text is in GR4; OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR7; OK §1985:XII.2.3 SR2.
